title: Tune availability without hiding convergence debt
description: Set N, R, and W, remove primary replicas, then decide whether fallback vnodes may answer. The workbench separates client success, quorum overlap, temporary placement, and recovery work.

modes.label: Sloppy quorum
modes.detail: Fallback vnodes may satisfy R or W when primary positions are unavailable. PR and PW are both zero.

modes.label: Require one primary
modes.detail: Fallbacks may help, but at least one primary vnode must answer both reads and writes.

modes.label: Primary positions only
modes.detail: Do not count fallback placements. Availability now depends entirely on the original N primary positions.

incidents.label: All primary replicas reachable
incidents.detail: The coordinator can contact every primary position in the preference list.
incidents.recoveryNote: No hinted handoff is created because every primary position is available.

incidents.label: One primary replica offline
incidents.detail: A node or vnode in the primary preference list cannot answer, while later ring positions remain reachable.
incidents.recoveryNote: When the primary owner returns, hinted handoff must transfer the temporary copy back and drain before the cluster is fully converged.

incidents.label: Two primaries isolated
incidents.detail: Only one of the first three positions is reachable in the common N=3 design, but several fallback positions can still answer.
incidents.recoveryNote: The request may touch several fallback vnodes, increasing transfer work and the time during which replicas occupy non-primary positions.

incidents.label: Primaries and fallbacks constrained
incidents.detail: Two primary positions are unavailable and only one later ring position can accept temporary responsibility.
incidents.recoveryNote: Even sloppy quorum cannot invent reachable capacity. Partial writes and retries remain possible, so recovery needs evidence from the actual preference list.
